recovery_balance.meaning: HRV z-score minus load z-score; below 0 = load outpacing recovery

aerobic_decoupling_pct.note: first-half vs second-half efficiency drift; under 5% = aerobically sound

drivers: HRV is elevated (+5.3 ms vs baseline), but recovery balance is +2.12 — however, this reflects low acute load (124) not strong recovery: chronic load is high (210) and ACWR is critically low (0.5), indicating significant detraining stress; resting HR dropped (-1.8 bpm), yet training readiness avg is only 34/100 over 7 days with latest at 50; sleep average is 4.3h (below 7h on 15 of last 14 days); stress is down (-5.4), but insufficient to offset cumulative sleep debt and readiness deficit
readiness.guidance: The body is in a state of under-recovery masked by low recent load — do not increase intensity or volume until readiness avg rises above 65 and sleep stabilizes ≥6.5h/night.

monthly_review.summary: This month shows faster average pace and higher zone 4/5 representation than last month, but within a context of sharply reduced total volume and acute load — suggesting forced tapering rather than intentional peaking.
monthly_review.highlight: Despite fewer runs and lower volume, average pace improved by 20 sec/km — but this coincides with a 3.0% efficiency decline and elevated aerobic TE, revealing compromised economy under effort, consistent with fatigue rather than fitness gain.

goal_tracker.message: To match last month’s 61.0 km would require 5.2 km across up to 3 remaining sessions — but with training readiness averaging 34/100, sleep averaging only 4.3 hours, and recovery balance driven by low load not robust recovery, chasing this number risks reinforcing fatigue. Prioritize rest and readiness over volume.

insights.title: Sleep debt directly correlates with declining running economy
insights.body: Average sleep is 4.3h (15/14 nights <7h); during that period, rolling median running economy worsened from 253.9 to 262.2 ml O2/kg/km (+8.3 ml), while the most efficient recent run (234.6) occurred after the only night with full recovery time (0.0h recovery time reported, but HRV peaked at 70.0 ms that day).

insights.title: Low ACWR masks aerobic fragility
insights.body: ACWR is 0.5 — far below the safe 0.8–1.3 band — yet aerobic decoupling median is 6.66%, with two recent runs >11%, indicating accumulated fatigue is degrading endurance capacity even without recent load spikes.

insights.title: Zone 3 dominance undermines aerobic base integrity
insights.body: Zone 3 now accounts for 26% of this month’s work (up from 19% in May and 31% in June), while Zone 2 dropped to 34% (from 43% in May). Efficiency in Zone 3 (0.7508 m/beat) is notably lower than Zone 2 (0.7891), confirming suboptimal pacing distribution for a recreational runner building endurance.

insights.title: Vertical oscillation increased as sleep declined
insights.body: Vertical oscillation averaged 7.9 cm across recent runs — up from 7.5–7.7 cm in March–May — and correlates with the 0.1h sleep decline vs baseline; higher vertical cost contributes directly to the observed rise in running economy (worsening values).

recommendations.action: Complete 3 days of zero running with strict sleep hygiene: bedtime by 22:00, no screens after 21:00, and morning HRV check before any activity
recommendations.reason: Training readiness avg is 34/100 and sleep debt is chronic — neural and autonomic recovery must precede physical loading

recommendations.action: On Day 4, perform 30 min Zone 1 walk or elliptical (HR ≤115 bpm), cadence ≥160 spm, vertical oscillation target <6.5 cm (use real-time form cues)
recommendations.reason: To re-establish neuromuscular coordination and metabolic efficiency without cardiac or mechanical stress

recommendations.action: On Day 6, complete 4 km easy run at Zone 2 (HR 125–135 bpm), focusing on stride length consistency (target ±1 cm) and ground contact <305 ms
recommendations.reason: Reintroduces running stimulus only after HRV sustains ≥68 ms for 2+ days and readiness score exceeds 60

risk_flags.risk: Chronic sleep debt driving biomechanical inefficiency
risk_flags.evidence: 15 of last 14 days with <7h sleep; vertical oscillation rose to 7.9 cm (from 7.5 cm baseline); running economy worsened by 8.3 ml O2/kg/km
risk_flags.action: Enforce non-negotiable 7h sleep window for next 7 days, verified via Garmin sleep staging

risk_flags.risk: Aerobic decoupling trending upward despite low load
risk_flags.evidence: Median decoupling = 6.66%, latest = 0.84% (an outlier), but 4 of last 6 runs >6%; VO2max stable at 39.5 yet efficiency declining
risk_flags.action: Pause all Zone 3+ efforts until decoupling median falls below 4.5% for 3 consecutive runs

risk_flags.evidence: Garmin status = PEAKING_1, yet readiness avg = 34/100, recovery balance = +2.12 (driven by load crash, not HRV surge), and body battery avg = 64.1 (down from 72+ in April)
risk_flags.action: Reset readiness algorithm by completing 3 full nights ≥7h sleep and 2 HRV-consistent mornings (≥68 ms)

weekly_focus.description: Shift focus from output metrics (pace, distance) to input fidelity (sleep duration, HRV stability, mechanical consistency) — using low-stimulus movement to rebuild autonomic regulation and movement economy before reintroducing running-specific load.
suggested_sessions: Zone 2 reconnection run (strict HR cap, stride focus)
